instructions.question: What role does sentence `sentences.$sentence` have in this dictated note?
instructions.focus: Read the original transcript and all sentence spans together. Classify from the words; never change their order or wording. The first sentence can itself be a list item. Existing lists and paragraph boundaries are retained by code. Do not infer missing words or punctuation.

continues.what: Continues the point of the previous sentence: running prose, an elaboration, an example, a reason or a follow-up. Also the first sentence of a note.
continues.not_for: A sentence that moves on to a new point, or that is one entry of a list.

new_paragraph.what: Moves on to a new point, step, request or aspect, where a writer would start a new paragraph to keep the note easy to read. A whole note often stays on one topic; its points still get their own paragraphs.
new_paragraph.not_for: The first sentence, or a sentence that elaborates on, gives an example of, or answers the previous one.
examples: Okay, now the second thing I want to talk about is the settings page.
So overall, what I'm really saying is that the tone has to change.

numbered_item.what: One entry in a counted or ordered sequence, such as steps, or entries introduced with first, second, one, two, three, firstly, secondly, next, finally.
numbered_item.not_for: A sentence that merely mentions a number or an order.
examples: First of all, we don't want to make it very long.
Secondly, we want to add tags.
Three, I don't see any formatting.

bullet_item.what: One entry in a list of parallel items without an order, such as names, products, options or features, each said as its own sentence.
bullet_item.not_for: A sentence that names several things in passing, or ordinary prose.
